summary: Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His career includes posts as Professor emeritus at the University of Delhi and Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, both attested in 2026.

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at University Maharani College and the University of Allahabad under Madhusudan Ojha, Shashadhar Tarkachuramani, and Arthur Venis, he served as librarian, Principal, and department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Gordon Dester Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. Kaufman held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University, where he was Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity from 1963.

Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) worked in history, archaeology, sinology, and linguistics. After studying at Dean Close School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, he served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from circa 1923 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson (born 1943) is a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He held fellowships at Trinity and Selwyn College, served as President of Wolfson College, Cambridge, and was President of the Royal Asiatic Society from 2015 to 2018.

Gore Ouseley (1770–1844) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He served at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (circa 1810–1814) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society from circa 1823 to 1844.

Gottfried Bernhardy (1800–1875) specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. Educated at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin, he spent the bulk of his career at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck (1762–1824) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and later held a post at Vilnius University (Imperial University of Vilna) from circa 1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) worked in linguistics and related fields. Educated at the universities of Leipzig and Jena, he taught at the University of Leipzig as professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

Gottfried Kinkel (1815–1882) was a scholar in history and archaeology and other fields. He studied at the University of Bonn, where he also held a post from circa 1840 to 1848, before serving at ETH Zurich from circa 1866 to 1882.

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer (1694–1738) specialized in sinology and history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Königsberg under Christoph Theodosius Walther, he taught in Königsberg and served as a professor at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences from 1726.

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at King's College London and Heidelberg University, he taught at King's College, served as Principal of Government College Lahore, and co-founded the University of the Punjab.

Gouriswar Bhattacharya (1924–2013) worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. His career included serving as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin, with affiliations attested in 2007 and 2026.

Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Rajasthan and the University of Allahabad, and chaired the Allahabad Museum and IIAS.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) was an Indologist and sociologist. He studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon, and served as sociology department head at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India and the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and later as Consultant for Epigraphy at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Govind Vinayak Devasthali (1906–1996) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. He held positions as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He held posts as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957), where he succeeded Benoytosh Bhattacharyya.

Grace S. Fong (born 1948) is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She held a professorship at Smith College (circa 1985–1989) before becoming associate professor and department chair at McGill University circa 1997.

Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (circa 1971–1978) and served as a lecturer at McMaster University from circa 1977 to 2003.
